title: Measure contrast instead of trusting a mockup
goal: Test actual foreground/background colours and document what contrast cannot prove.
explanation: A generated interface image cannot establish accessibility. Extract or choose actual colour values and calculate contrast using the WCAG relative-luminance formula. Ordinary text generally needs 4.5:1 at WCAG AA; large text has a 3:1 threshold, but meeting a ratio alone does not address keyboard access, labels or screen-reader semantics.
sampleInput: Test pairs: white #FFFFFF on burgundy #7C1F16; warm grey #84766A on cream #FDF7EE; gold #D4971B on cream #FDF7EE. Use the activity calculator to measure each pair, then choose colours for an actual editable heading and button.
prompt: Suggest an accessible-looking page concept, but label it a visual concept only. Separately propose exact hex foreground/background pairs for ordinary text. I will measure the actual contrast and test labels and keyboard access myself. Do not claim neon colours or a screenshot guarantee WCAG compliance.
workedExample: White on the dark burgundy produces a strong text contrast. Gold on cream is much weaker and should not be assumed suitable for ordinary small text. Record the calculator’s numeric result and threshold rather than trusting colour names or visual excitement.

steps.title: Choose actual colours
steps.text: Use the supplied pairs, not an image generator’s verbal claim.

steps.title: Calculate each ratio
steps.text: Run the local deterministic calculator and save the numeric results.

steps.title: Apply a threshold
steps.text: Use 4.5:1 for ordinary text and explain when a genuinely large-text threshold may apply.

steps.title: Revise a failing pair
steps.text: Darken the foreground or lighten the background, then measure again.

steps.title: Inspect beyond contrast
steps.text: Write separate checks for labels, focus visibility, keyboard order and information not conveyed by colour alone.

checks: All three original colour pairs have measured ratios and ordinary-text pass/fail results.
A revised failing pair is measured again instead of judged by eye.
The final report explicitly separates contrast from complete accessibility compliance.
commonMistakes: Equating neon/high saturation with sufficient contrast.
Claiming an image mockup proves screen-reader or keyboard accessibility.
offline: Use the formula/known examples in the handbook to annotate a design. Mark unmeasured pairs as unverified.
reflection: Which accessibility problem would remain even after every colour pair passed?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. All three original colour pairs have measured ratios and ordinary-text pass/fail results.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. A revised failing pair is measured again instead of judged by eye.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Equating neon/high saturation with sufficient contrast.
